message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the 2003 Mr. Basketball America and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). Known for his combination of size, athleticism, court vision, and basketball IQ, he has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams and All‑Star games, and he has been named an NBA All‑Star MVP multiple times.

Beyond the court, LeBron is a prominent philanthropist and entrepreneur. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which has donated millions to education initiatives, most notably the opening of the “I Promise School” in Akron. He also has a media company, SpringHill Entertainment, and has produced films and television shows, including the critically acclaimed series “The Book of Boba Fett.” LeBron’s influence extends into social activism, where he has spoken out on issues such as racial justice, voting rights, and education reform.
